title: Household Vehicle Count and the Multi-Car Discount, Cardinal Personal Auto Policy Rating Rule
content:
On the Cardinal Personal Auto Policy, the multi-car discount is decided by the household's vehicle count, not by the single policy's.

## Rule

- **Household vehicle count.** The number of vehicles scheduled across every Cardinal Personal Auto Policy of the customer whose status is bound, in force or cancel pending, measured on the rating date.
- **Threshold.** When that count is 2 or more, every policy of the customer receives its own package's multi-car discount percentage. When the count is one, no policy receives it.
- **Effect across policies.** Because the count spans policies, adding a vehicle to one policy or removing one from it can switch the multi-car discount on or off on the customer's other policy. That other policy is then re-rated from the same effective date, and its own additional or return premium is written against it.
- **Vehicle cap.** The per-policy vehicle cap is the vehicle maximum of each policy's own package. It is never pooled across policies.

## Condition and result

| Household vehicle count on the rating date | Multi-car discount |
|---|---|
| 1 | Not received by any of the customer's policies |
| 2 or more | Received by every policy of the customer, each at its own package's percentage |

## Hypothetical cases

- A customer holds one in-force policy with one vehicle and one bound policy with one vehicle. The household count is 2, so both policies receive their own package's multi-car discount.
- That customer removes the only vehicle on the bound policy. The count falls to 1, the multi-car discount switches off on the remaining policy, and that policy is re-rated from the same effective date, with its own additional premium written against it.
- A customer has one expired policy with two vehicles and one in-force policy with one vehicle. The expired policy does not count, so the household count is 1.
- A Cardinal Auto Basic policy with 4 vehicles is at its own cap even if the customer's other policy schedules fewer vehicles than its cap allows; caps are not pooled.
